slides.title: Introduction to Operators
slides.content: Operators perform operations on variables and values. C# includes arithmetic, assignment, comparison, and logical operators.

exercise.prompt: Which category does the + operator belong to?

slides.title: Arithmetic Operators
slides.example:
int sum = 10 + 5;    // 15
int diff = 10 - 5;   // 5
int prod = 10 * 5;   // 50
int rem = 10 % 3;    // 1

exercise.prompt: What operator gives the remainder of division?

slides.title: Assignment Operators
slides.content: Assignment operators store values. += adds and assigns, -= subtracts and assigns, *= multiplies and assigns, and /= divides and assigns.

slides.title: Comparison Operators
slides.content: Comparison operators compare two values and return a bool: == (equal), != (not equal), >, <, >=, <=.

slides.title: Logical Operators
slides.content: Logical operators combine boolean expressions: && (AND), || (OR), and ! (NOT). && and || use short-circuit evaluation.

exercise.prompt: What is the logical AND operator?

slides.title: Increment and Decrement
slides.content: ++ increments by 1, -- decrements by 1. They can be used as prefix (++x) or postfix (x++), affecting evaluation order.

slides.title: Operator Precedence
slides.content: Operators follow precedence rules: multiplicative (* / %) before additive (+ -), which are before comparison (== !=), which are before logical (&& ||). Use parentheses to override.
slides.example:
int result = 2 + 3 * 4; // 14, not 20
bool test = (2 + 3) == 5; // true

exercise.prompt: Add parentheses to make the expression evaluate to true: 5 + 3 * 2 == 11.

slides.title: Practice: Operators
slides.content: Combine arithmetic, assignment, comparison, and logical operators to solve problems. Remember operator precedence and use parentheses for clarity.

exercise.prompt: Declare int a=10, b=3. Print a+b, a-b, a*b, a/b, and a%b on separate lines.
hints: Make sure your code includes the required keywords/elements: class, static
When run, your code should output: 13, 7, 30, 3, 1

slides.title: Flow Builder: Operators
slides.content: Use the Flow Builder to add two numbers and output the result.

exercise.prompt: Build a flow that declares int a=10, b=3, computes a+b, and outputs it
